Three actually drawn staging panels establish alarm, quiet aftermath and mulch tribunal with supported dogs, understandable chair occlusion and coherent domestic perspective. Finished images retain those distinct roles.

findings: Native 1536x1024 opened in full. Neet has continuous full narrow torso, fine separated legs, four grounded paws, broad triangular ears, projecting muzzle and near-flush nub. Small foreground-to-midground scale is coherent with bin and chair.

Buddy head connects through neck and chest to chair-occluded body. Visible forelegs and hindfoot have plausible ownership and ground contact; wooden chair members remain distinct from legs. The slim dark tail is visible beside the chair.

Both short body coats are smooth color areas without curly engraved strokes or raised shag. Buddy retains pale projecting irregular moustache, chin beard, brows, hanging ear fringe and modest paw furnishing.

Raccoon is supported on closed bin lid. Neet directs attention left toward it; Buddy peeks with closed mouth from shelter. Heather holds mug. The broad distance between danger and chair makes the conflicting responses legible. Arrival state contains no premature fight or verdict.

Native 1448x1086 opened in full. Neet carries a full connected torso over four separately readable fine legs and supported feet; large ears, cream chest, modest head and tiny nub match reference identity.

Buddy has a real neck, deep chest, continuous trunk behind chair, substantial legs and clear space below body. Three feet are visible and the remaining hindleg can plausibly be chair-occluded. No detached paw or chair fusion found. His tail extends from the rump with a narrow dark taper and modest fringe.

Smooth broad light/shadow areas now cover tan and gray torsos and thighs. No curly interior coat marks remain. Buddy facial furnishings remain visibly projecting and irregular, with restrained chin beard and regional ear and paw strands.

Raccoon is absent and fence empty. Proud forward Neet and Buddy emerging from his shelter preserve the aftermath joke; mug on ledge agrees with preceding prose. Closer composition contributes consequence rather than repeating the wide alarm tableau.

Native 1536x1024 opened in full. Both seated dogs have continuous head-neck-chest-pelvis construction. Neet forelegs are fine and straight with grounded forefeet; folded hindquarters and hindfeet are connected. Buddy substantial forelegs and folded hindlegs also rest on rug without floating or duplicate limbs.

Neet keeps broad ears, modest projecting face, tan short body and cream chest. Buddy pale moustache projects beyond dark muzzle, with separate modest chin beard, light brows and hanging ear furnishings. His torso remains smooth and close-coated; angular tonal boundaries are broad wash shapes rather than curly engraved hair.

Buddy visible dark tail is a relatively slender taper with limited end fringe, not a full plume; it attaches to the seated rump. Neither body has the earlier raised shag contour. Small regional paw strands remain appropriate.

Neet looks upward to Sagar while Buddy looks down toward the single mulch chip on rug. Sagar hands stay resting and Heather is seated without applause. This preserves anticipation before verdict. Ordinary warm living room and consistent chair/rug perspective support the domestic setting; humans remain provisional.

Tribunal tail is tapered with limited fringe rather than broad plume. Acceptance applies only to these pinned replacements.
